headline: Africa: Sudan: Drone Attacks Kill Civilians and Cripple Sudan's Power Infrastructure, UN Warns of Growing Humanitarian Toll
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

- Africa: Sudan: Drone Attacks Kill Civilians and Cripple Sudan's Power Infrastructure, UN Warns of Growing Humanitarian Toll.

The Caribbean - bottom line: Renewed push for OSH Bill - Government targets fiscal-year deadline for tabling long-delayed legislation.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Renewed push for OSH Bill - Government targets fiscal-year deadline for tabling long-delayed legislation.
After years of delays, attention has returned to the much-anticipated Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Bill, with renewed efforts to advance the legislation towards passage. The issue came into focus yesterday at the launch by Jamaicans for Justice (JFJ) of its handbook, titled A Human Rights Approach to Occupational Safety and Health in the Workplace. JFJ said the manual addresses gaps in workplace health policies, moving beyond an HIV/AIDS-only approach to embrace a more comprehensive health framework.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Pathways trial nears verdict.
The prosecution and defence in the Pathways International murder trial are expected to make their closing arguments today, bringing the case against murder accused Andre Ruddock closer to a verdict. The defence closed its case yesterday, calling only Ruddock, despite previously indicating that it intended to call another witness. The 36-year-old farmer and security guard is being tried for the murder of Taneka Gardner, who was killed on October 17, 2021, at the Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries in St James.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Trump says Hegseth doing 'a very good job' as questions swirl about defence secretary's future.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 12 hours ago: Trump says Hegseth doing 'a very good job' as questions swirl about defence secretary's future.
US President Donald Trump backed Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth a day after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in midterm elections that reflected voter anger over the war on Iran. Asked whether he was considering replacing Hegseth, whom he has described as a champion of the war, Trump told reporters: “No, I think he’s doing a very good job.” The response contrasted with then-president George Bush, who fired Defence Secretary Donald Rumsfeld the morning after the 2006 midterm elections, when voter discontent over the Iraq war helped Democrats win control of Congress.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Trump faces new political reality as Democrats vow investigations.
President Donald Trump was left to grapple on Thursday with the stinging rebuke from voters after a midterm election rout, while triumphant Democrats vowed to lower prices and combat the “cartel” within the White House in the new Congress. Trump faces a radically transformed and hostile political landscape after Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate in Tuesday’s midterms.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Taipei Times, The Hindu - International, Africanews, just now: Largely peaceful marches take place across France as workers stage strike.
Some protesters clashed with police in Paris and Lyon on Thursday during largely peaceful nationwide demonstrations and a one-day strike by some public sector workers in a renewed challenge to President Emmanuel Macron. The protests were attended by several high-profile politicians, including presidential candidates Jean-Luc Melenchon and Raphael Glucksmann. They follow demonstrations over living costs, public services and education that have triggered the worst civil unrest France has seen in years.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 12 hours ago: North Korea says it tested air-defence missile, staged cruise missile drill.
North Korea test-fired a newly designed air-defence missile system and staged a cruise missile strike drill on Wednesday, state media KCNA reported on Thursday. KCNA said the air-defence test confirmed the technical specifications and reliability of the missile’s new materials and multiple guidance modes. It also confirmed the system’s ability to identify and track targets, KCNA said. A sub-unit of North Korea’s long-range strategic cruise missile unit in the east also struck a virtual airport target in a drill on Wednesday, KCNA said.

Its mobile launch capability introduces tactical flexibility, posing significant challenges for enemy defense systems.
